mission: Forethought researches what happens when AI can replace human researchers and a century of technological progress gets compressed into years. It studies the 'grand challenges' this would throw up — AI-enabled coups, new weapons, digital minds, space resources — and what we can do now to prepare. It was co-founded by Max Dalton, Will MacAskill, Tom Davidson and Amrit Sidhu-Brar.

key_work.title: Preparing for the Intelligence Explosion
key_work.plain_summary: Argues AI could drive a century of progress in a few years, forcing many hard-to-reverse decisions in quick succession — so preparing is about much more than alignment.

key_work.title: AI-Enabled Coups: How a Small Group Could Use AI to Seize Power
key_work.plain_summary: Explains how a tiny group — even one person — controlling advanced AI could seize power, and suggests safeguards for labs and governments.

key_work.title: Will AI R&D Automation Cause a Software Intelligence Explosion?
key_work.plain_summary: Asks whether AI that improves AI software could set off runaway progress even without more computer chips, and weighs the evidence.

key_work.title: Better Futures (series)
key_work.plain_summary: A series by Will MacAskill on how to make the long-term future go well, not just avoid catastrophe.

key_work.title: AI Tools for Existential Security
key_work.plain_summary: Identifies AI applications — for forecasting, coordination and epistemics — worth accelerating because they help humanity handle the transition safely.

warnings.text: When AI can substitute for human researchers, a century's worth of progress could be compressed into years.
New technologies could arrive in quick succession: miracle drugs and new bioweapons, automated companies and automated militaries.
A small group, or even one person, could use advanced AI to seize power.
Hard-to-reverse decisions cannot always be safely delegated to future AI systems.

recommendations.text: Prepare now for the range of 'grand challenges' an intelligence explosion would bring, not just alignment.
Guard against AI-enabled coups, e.g. by requiring AI systems to follow rules that prevent illegitimate power grabs.
Procure AI for critical systems from multiple independent providers.
Accelerate AI tools that improve collective reasoning and coordination.
